newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares lower in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued their downtrend on Sunday in quiet trade which was partly affected by the absence of foreign players, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index fell 2.47 points to close at 396.85 against 399.32 points on Thursday. Turnover was a low 48.5 million pounds ($14.3 million).
"Dealings by foreign funds form between 20-25 percent of total trade now. So the market is affected on Sundays," said broker Mohamed Magdi at EFG/Hermes.

Cement and housing firms again top the list of active shares. Helwan Portland Cement shares fell .11 pounds to close at 79.15 in trade worth 4.3 million pounds, making it the most active share of the day.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the most active housing firm, with shares worth 3.94 million pounds changing hands. It ended down 3.00 pounds at 498.
Cairo Housing and Development shed 0.05 pounds to close at 23.55 pounds after 3.44 million pounds worth of shares were traded.
Amriyah Cement, one of the best performing cement firms, continued its uptrend, rising 3.5 to end at 88.50 pounds.
"Amriyah is in very large demand," Magdi said.
All active millers went down. East Delta Flour Mills lost 2.35 pounds to 85.55, Central and West Delta Flour Mills fell 2.52 to 106.5 and Upper Egypt Flour Mills 0.95 to close at 91 pounds.
"People are either taking profit or afraid of the market and trying to get out,"Magdi said.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 640.85 from 651.23 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms was marginally up at 267.22 points from 267.15.
Out of the 77 shares traded, 25 gained, 36 lost and 16 ended the day unchanged.
